subtitle: Install and enable the capabilities you need to give Vetta more expertise

banner.title: Extend with capabilities
banner.description: This page lists skills and connectors. Pick what you want to accomplish and add it in one click to use it in chat.

searchAdd.title: Search and add
searchAdd.description: Search to find a capability quickly, or use Add to import a local Skill / plugin or configure an MCP connector.

scope.title: Public / Personal
scope.description: Public browses available capabilities and Vetta built-in abilities. Personal manages universal skills and manually installed capabilities — enable, configure, or remove.

list.title: Capability cards
list.description: Each card is one capability. View details, add or enable it; you will be prompted when credentials are required.

create-skill.name: Create Skill
create-skill.description: Create or update an Agent Skill that follows the Vetta spec: place the files, register it in skills-manifest.json, or update the plugin config.

install-ability.name: Install Ability
install-ability.description: Install plugins, Skills/scenes, and MCP servers into this machine's Vetta, reloading right away when a plugin upgrade leaves a pending version.

publish-ability.name: Publish Ability
publish-ability.description: Submit a skill, scene, MCP server, plugin, or ability bundle to the Vetta marketplace, covering required fields, localization, and the review flow.

report-canvas.name: Canvas report
report-canvas.description: When the user wants a standalone report, audit board, or long-form analysis, write it with artifact to Canvas instead of chat-only Markdown.

architecture-canvas.name: Architecture canvas
architecture-canvas.description: When the user wants an architecture, module, or system diagram, create an HTML canvas artifact with inline SVG instead of pasting an image in chat.

chart-canvas.name: Data chart
chart-canvas.description: When the user wants a trend, comparison, or share-of-total chart, write the declarative chart JSON with artifact so Canvas renders it natively instead of listing numbers in chat.

review-canvas.name: Change review
review-canvas.description: When the user wants a cross-file code review, write the full unified diff with artifact so Canvas groups it by file with line stats.

database-analysis.name: Database questions & analysis
database-analysis.description: Ask questions about connected databases and analyze metrics, trends, breakdowns, and period comparisons. Read-only by default, with definitions and query evidence.

ap-router.name: Adaptive pipeline router
ap-router.description: At the start of any build task, grade its weight, print a one-line workflow plan, and decide whether each stage runs in this session or is delegated to a subagent.

ap-prototype.name: Prototype & requirements
ap-prototype.description: Turn an idea into a single-file interactive HTML prototype plus a one-page requirements sheet (R# items, F# field lists, A# acceptance) so the direction is confirmed before any code.

ap-design.name: Design notes
ap-design.description: Turn confirmed requirements into a one-page design.md with a file-level change list, architecture decisions, and risks; no business code in this stage.

ap-dev.name: Development execution
ap-dev.description: Execute coding with the change list first, incrementally and verifiably in dependency order, with self-tests, call-chain review, and a structured report.

ap-test.name: Pipeline testing
ap-test.description: Verify basic functionality within a minutes-level budget: project health check, targeted executable cases, and a user-perspective checklist; writes test-report.md.

ap-contract.name: Subagent contract template
ap-contract.description: Assemble the spawn_agent task contract aligned with its actual slots before delegating a pipeline stage to a general subagent; the contract is the subagent's entire input.
